reason: Tok.str joins str() of the elements (:143); UnstructuredSpec proves str(get_unstructured(v)) == v when no encoded word decodes, and UnstructuredEncodedWords now also pins the join through EncodedWord and EWWhiteSpaceTerminal elements ('=?utf-8?q?a?= =?utf-8?q?b?=' gives 'ab' on 3.15.2).

name: BareQuotedString.__str__
reason: Unchanged: Tok.str gives quote_string of the joined elements (:278); QuotingRoundTrip pins it and the reparse refutation (bug textlibs-email-quoted-string-reparse) records that it drops the backslash hiding an encoded word.

name: BareQuotedString.value
reason: Unchanged: valueF gives strs of the elements (:282), and QuotingRoundTrip pins value == s for text with whitespace runs, which the generic TokenList.value would collapse.

name: Comment.__str__
reason: CommentSpec, which now credits it, claims str(c) == '(' + b.render + ')' for comment bodies of every nesting depth, but Tok.str/commentStrs recurse with no recursion limit while CPython's Comment.__str__ -> quote -> str(nested) raises RecursionError by depth 600 (500 still works) ('('*600 + ')'*600 parses, str() raises on 3.15.2), so a proven statement is false; QuotingRoundTrip alone still holds, and bounding the nesting depth (or modelling frames as the tomllib model does) would restore the row.

name: Comment.quote
reason: The comment branch (:297-298) is now reached, by CommentSpec's nested bodies (a quote that escaped nested comments fails str() == '(' + b.render + ')'), but that statement is false by nesting depth 600 (500 still works), where str(value) of the nested comment raises RecursionError on 3.15.2 and the model, which has no recursion limit, returns the text.

name: Comment.content
reason: CommentSpec claims content == b.content (nested comments as written) for every nesting depth, but ''.join(str(x) for x in self) recurses through Comment.__str__ and raises RecursionError by depth 600 (500 still works) on 3.15.2 while commentContent/strs return; QuotingRoundTrip's flat case still holds.

name: get_encoded_word
reason: getEncodedWord/ewHexFix/ewBuild follow :1084-1127, but UnstructuredEncodedWords only reaches the plain success path: GoodTok forbids '?=' in the token and every word is followed by whitespace or the end, so the =XX re-split of :1093-1099 (taken by every Q word whose text starts with an escape, '=?utf-8?q?=C3=A9?=' gives 'é' on 3.15.2) is never run, and the EncodedWord's own defects (whitespace inside, decode's defects, missing trailing whitespace) are never inspected; a get_encoded_word without the re-split or without any defect satisfies every entry.

name: get_unstructured
reason: UnstructuredEncodedWords now pins decoded EncodedWords and the EWWhiteSpaceTerminal between two of them, but every value it covers starts with an encoded word and alternates with whitespace, and UnstructuredSpec has no word that decodes, so the 'missing whitespace before encoded word' defect and have_ws=False (:1170-1174, 'a=?utf-8?q?b?=') and the unstructured[-2] == 'encoded-word' test (:1175-1178, 'x =?utf-8?q?b?=' keeps its space on 3.15.2) are unpinned: a get_unstructured that turned every fws before an encoded word into an EWWhiteSpaceTerminal, or never added the defect, satisfies both entries.
